insights.topic: Verified purchase data vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl's beta has processed $2.17M in confirmed GMV across 37,576+ receipts — each one a cryptographically verified transaction, not an inferred intent signal. For brands paying $5+ CPM on probabilistic audiences, this represents a structural alternative: deterministic purchase proof at the SKU and merchant level.

The 14-day rolling window is running at 5,435 receipts and $261,205 as of June 29 — accumulating at roughly 360–380 receipts per day with a consistent evening acceleration pattern (sharpest gains 16:15–20:15 UTC). That cadence reflects a real, active shopper panel, not a static dataset.

insights.topic: Category mix: grocery and dining dominate verified volume
insights.insight: Grocery-supermarkets (1,426 receipts, ~$47.87 average basket) and restaurants-dining (1,297 receipts, ~$37.77 average basket) together account for 50.2% of 14-day receipt volume and are gaining share. CPG and QSR brands looking for purchase-verified audience segments are targeting the categories where verified signal is densest.

insights.topic: Top retailer concentration signals where shoppers are verifying
insights.insight: Walmart leads the 14-day brand distribution at 370 receipts, followed by Costco (166) and Target (132) — mass-market and warehouse formats dominating verified volume. Brands competing for share at these retailers now have a confirmed-purchase data layer to measure against, not a modeled proxy.

insights.topic: Average basket compression is category-mix driven, not demand softness
insights.insight: Average basket has compressed from ~$65 to ~$48 over the monitoring window, tracking the shift toward grocery and dining receipts — categories that carry lower per-transaction values than department or home improvement retail. Marketers should read this as audience composition change, not weakening consumer spend.

The rolling 14-day window drops 290–325 receipts at each UTC midnight boundary as the oldest day ages out — but all ten confirmed rollovers have recovered within 4 hours, at 28–35 receipts per hour. The absence of any recovery failure indicates a stable, continuously contributing shopper base rather than a burst-and-lapse panel.
